examples.ko: 같은 값이면 다홍치마니까 더 큰 방을 골랐어요.
examples.en: If the price is the same, you might as well take the better one, so I chose the bigger room.

examples.ko: 가격이 같으면 다홍치마라고 색이 예쁜 쪽을 샀어요.
examples.en: Since the price was the same, I bought the prettier-colored one.

examples.ko: 같은 값이면 다홍치마라서 포장이 좋은 선물을 골랐어요.
examples.en: As the price was the same, I picked the gift with nicer wrapping.

examples.ko: 같은 값이면 다홍치마인데 왜 그걸 안 사요?
examples.en: If it costs the same, why not buy the better one?

examples.ko: 같은 값이면 다홍치마지요, 이왕이면 새 걸로 해요.
examples.en: Same price, so go for the better one. Let's get a new one.

examples.ko: 같은 값이면 다홍치마라는 말처럼 보기 좋은 상품이 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: As the saying goes, good-looking products are more popular.

explain: 거의 항상 속담 '같은 값이면 다홍치마'로 써요. 값이 같다면 겉모습이나 조건이 더 좋은 쪽을 고른다는 말이에요. 말할 때는 '이왕이면'과 비슷하게 가볍게 써요.

phrases.example: 같은 값이면 다홍치마라는데, 이왕이면 색이 예쁜 걸 사요.
phrases.en: They say if it costs the same, get the nicer one, so let's buy the prettier color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값이 같을 때 더 좋은 쪽을 고르자는 속담이에요. 치마 이야기가 아니라 물건, 선택 전반에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that when the price is equal, choose the better option. It is not about skirts but about any choice.
phrases.en_equiv: may as well get the better one

explain_en: It is almost always used inside the proverb '같은 값이면 다홍치마'. It means that if the price is the same, you pick the one that looks or is better. In speech it works lightly, much like '이왕이면'.

examples.en: The child shakes its head, saying it doesn't want to eat.
When I asked him, he shook his head without a word.

examples.ko: 동생은 안 간다며 계속 도리질하고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling keeps shaking their head, saying they won't go.
Even when I asked, she shook her head and refused.
The way the baby shakes its head is so cute.
Even though my friend shook his head, I did not give up.

explain: '도리질을 하다'와 같은 뜻이고, 싫다·아니다·거절한다는 마음을 고개로 보여 줄 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '고개를 젓다'가 더 흔한 말투예요.

phrases.en: The child shook her head at the medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거의 일을 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past form for telling what happened.

phrases.en: My younger sibling said he wouldn't go, shaking his head.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말과 고개 흔들기가 동시에 일어나는 장면에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For scenes where speech and head shaking happen at once.

phrases.en: She shook her head instead of answering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 일상 대화에서 더 자연스럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but it sounds more natural in daily talk.

explain_en: Cute, childlike head shaking to refuse; also used for babies (도리질) It means the same as '도리질을 하다' and is used when you show refusal or disagreement with your head. In everyday talk, '고개를 젓다' is the more usual way to say it.

t90.ax: The way the baby shakes its head is so cute.

en: to be stripped; to be denuded

examples.en: The baby runs around the yard with nothing on.
A naked child is laughing in the bathhouse.

examples.ko: 동화 속 임금님은 벌거벗은 채로 거리를 걸었어요.
examples.en: The king in the fairy tale walked down the street naked.
Some people sleep with nothing on because it is hot.
In winter the bare trees look lonely.
They are planting trees on the bare mountain.

explain: 아기나 동화 속 인물에는 자연스럽지만, 어른에게 쓰면 아주 직접적으로 들려요. 같은 뜻의 '알몸'은 명사라서 '알몸으로'라고 하고, 벌거벗다는 '벌거벗은 채로'처럼 동사로 써요. 나무가 없는 산에도 '벌거벗은 산'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The baby is laughing without any clothes on.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-은 채로'는 그 상태 그대로 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-은 채로' means staying in that state.

phrases.en: With no trees, it became a bare mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무나 풀이 없는 산을 비유로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative way to describe a mountain with no trees or grass.

phrases.en: Children play in the water without clothes in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주로 어린아이에게 쓰는 말투예요. 어른에게는 직접적으로 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mostly used for small children; it sounds very direct for adults.

explain_en: It sounds natural for a baby or a fairy-tale figure, but very direct for an adult. '알몸' is a noun ('알몸으로'), while 벌거벗다 is a verb ('벌거벗은 채로'). It is also used for a treeless mountain: '벌거벗은 산'.

t90.ax: In winter the bare trees look lonely.

examples.en: My younger sibling went into the room with a pout.
The child is pouting, as if about to cry.

examples.ko: 못마땅한 듯 비쭉거리지 말고 말로 해요.
examples.en: Don't pout in disapproval; say it with words.
When she got scolded, my daughter pouted her lips.
The way she pouted was cute.
He kept pouting and finally burst into tears.

explain: 불만이 있거나 울음이 나오려고 할 때 입을 삐죽 내밀고 움직이는 모습이에요. 보통 '입을 비쭉거리다'로 쓰고 '삐죽거리다'라고도 해요. 아이 같은 모습을 말할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My younger brother pouted and sulked.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비쭉거리다'와 같은 뜻으로 더 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 비쭉거리다 and more commonly used.

phrases.en: The child is pouting his lips.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비쭉거리다'와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word that can replace 비쭉거리다.

phrases.en: The child complained with a pout.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입을 내밀면서 말하는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes speaking while pushing out one's lips.

explain_en: It describes pushing out and moving the lips when you are dissatisfied or about to cry. It is usually used as '입을 비쭉거리다' and is also said as '삐죽거리다'. It often appears when describing a child-like look.

t90.ax: The way she pouted was cute.

examples.en: His mouth twitched, perhaps because he was angry.

examples.ko: 웃음을 참느라 제 입술이 자꾸 실룩거려요.
examples.en: My lips keep twitching because I'm holding back laughter.
He sniffed, twitching his nose.

examples.ko: 눈 밑이 실룩거리는 건 피곤해서 그런가 봐요.
examples.en: The twitching under my eye must be because I'm tired.

examples.ko: 강아지가 코를 실룩거릴 때 정말 귀여워요.
examples.en: The puppy is so cute when it twitches its nose.

examples.ko: 아이가 입을 실룩거리고 있다가 결국 울음을 터뜨렸어요.
examples.en: The child was twitching its mouth and finally burst into tears.

explain: 입, 코, 눈 밑처럼 몸의 작은 부분이 씰룩씰룩 움직일 때 써요. '실룩이다'도 비슷하고, 소리가 더 센 '씰룩거리다'도 흔히 써요.

phrases.en: The corners of my mouth twitch because I'm holding back a laugh.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실룩거리다'보다 소리와 움직임이 더 센 느낌이고 일상에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds and feels a bit stronger than 실룩거리다 and is very common in daily speech.

phrases.example: 피곤해서 그런지 눈 밑이 자꾸 실룩거려요.
phrases.en: Maybe because I'm tired, the skin under my eye keeps twitching.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 작은 부분이 자기도 모르게 떨릴 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing for a small body part twitching involuntarily.
phrases.en_equiv: the skin under one's eye twitches

phrases.en: He held back his laughter, twitching his mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'를 붙여 다른 행동과 함께 일어나는 모습을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -며 lets you describe the twitching happening alongside another action.

explain_en: Standard form, neutral — lips or muscles moving repeatedly. It is used when a small part of the body, such as the mouth, nose or area under the eye, twitches. '실룩이다' is similar, and '씰룩거리다', with a stronger sound, is also commonly used.

examples.ko: 놀란 엄마가 아이를 안고 가슴을 쓸어내렸어요.
examples.en: The startled mother held her child and patted her own chest to calm down.

examples.ko: 할머니가 제 머리를 부드럽게 쓸어내려 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother gently stroked my hair down for me.
I smooth the wrinkles of my clothes down with my hand.

examples.ko: 다행히 아무도 안 다쳐서 가슴을 쓸어내리고 있어요.
examples.en: Luckily nobody was hurt, so I'm relieved and calming myself.
He laughed while stroking down his long beard.

examples.ko: 아이 등을 쓸어내리면 기침이 좀 가라앉아요.
examples.en: If you stroke the child's back downward, the cough settles a bit.

explain: 손바닥으로 위에서 아래로 천천히 문지르는 동작이에요. 몸의 부분이나 옷, 수염처럼 눈에 보이는 대상에 쓰고, '가슴을 쓸어내리다'는 안도할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.

phrases.example: 합격 소식을 듣고 그제야 가슴을 쓸어내렸어요.
phrases.en: Only after hearing I had passed did I finally breathe easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 걱정했던 일이 잘 끝나서 안심할 때 써요. 실제로 가슴을 만지지 않아도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you feel relieved that something you worried about turned out fine. You don't have to actually touch your chest.
phrases.en_equiv: to breathe a sigh of relief

explain_en: It describes slowly rubbing downward with the palm. It is used for visible things like body parts, clothes or a beard, and '가슴을 쓸어내리다' is an expression for feeling relieved.

en: to be fair-faced; to be radiant; to be bright

examples.ko: 그 배우는 웃을 때 얼굴이 해사해요.
examples.en: That actor's face looks radiant when he smiles.
The staff member who greeted us with a bright smile was impressive.
The baby waved with a bright, clear smile.
Since coming back from vacation, your face has become so fresh and bright.
He was a young man with a fair face and clear eyes.
Your skin looks so clear and bright, and I'm envious.

explain: 주로 사람의 얼굴이나 웃음이 맑고 깨끗하고 환할 때 쓰는 칭찬이에요. 일상 대화보다는 글이나 부드러운 말투에서 더 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: The baby is smiling with a bright, fair face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해사하다'를 명사 앞에 써서 맑고 환한 얼굴을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to praise a clear, bright face.

phrases.en: She greeted me with a bright smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형 '해사하게'로 웃는 모습을 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverbial form '해사하게' describes how someone smiles.

phrases.en: Your face looks really bright today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보이다'를 붙여 보기에 환하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds '-아/어 보이다' to say someone looks bright.

explain_en: It is a compliment mostly for a person's face or smile that looks clear, clean and bright. You hear it more in writing or a soft, gentle tone than in everyday casual talk.

examples.en: My grandmother was born and raised in a remote mountain village.

examples.ko: 두메산골이라 버스가 하루에 두 번밖에 안 와요.
examples.en: It's a remote mountain village, so the bus only comes twice a day.
Even remote mountain villages have the internet now.

examples.ko: 도시를 떠나 두메산골로 이사 갈까 해요.
examples.en: I'm thinking of leaving the city and moving to a remote mountain village.

examples.ko: 그 학교는 두메산골에 있는 작은 분교예요.
examples.en: That school is a small branch school in a remote mountain village.

examples.ko: 두메산골 마을에서 별이 정말 많이 보였어요.
examples.en: I could see so many stars in the remote mountain village.

explain: '시골'보다 더 깊고 외진 산속 마을을 말해요. 교통이 불편하고 사람이 적다는 느낌이 있어서, 옛날이야기나 어렸을 때 살던 곳을 말할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The remote mountain village has only one shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외진 산속 마을을 구체적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a specific remote mountain village.

phrases.en: I lived in a remote mountain village when I was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린 시절 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in stories about childhood.
phrases.en_equiv: to live in a remote mountain village

phrases.en: That actor comes from a remote mountain village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 고향을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to introduce where someone is from.

explain_en: It refers to a village deeper in the mountains and more isolated than a '시골' (countryside). It suggests poor transport and few people, and often comes up in old stories or when talking about where someone lived as a child.

en: back way; back lane; back street

examples.ko: 그 가수는 이제 역사의 뒤안길로 사라졌어요.
examples.en: That singer has now faded into the backwaters of history.

examples.ko: 골목 뒤안길을 따라 걸으면 조용한 집이 나와요.
examples.en: If you walk along the back lane, you'll come to a quiet house.

examples.ko: 인기가 식은 뒤 그는 뒤안길에서 조용히 지냈어요.
examples.en: After his popularity faded, he lived quietly out of the spotlight.

examples.ko: 화려한 도시의 뒤안길에는 힘든 사람들도 있어요.
examples.en: In the back lanes of the glamorous city, there are people struggling too.

examples.ko: 그 기술은 뒤안길로 밀려난 지 오래예요.
examples.en: That technology was pushed aside long ago.
I found an old restaurant on a back street of the market.

explain: 원래는 집 뒤쪽이나 큰길에서 벗어난 길이지만, 요즘은 '화려한 모습 뒤의 잊힌 곳'이라는 비유로 더 많이 써요. 주로 글이나 뉴스, 이야기체에서 보여요.

phrases.example: 그 가게는 시대가 바뀌면서 역사의 뒤안길로 사라졌어요.
phrases.en: The shop faded into history as times changed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한때 있었지만 이제는 사람들에게 잊힌 것에 써요. 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 굳은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that once existed but is now forgotten. It is a fixed expression often seen in writing and the news.

explain_en: It originally means the path behind a house or off the main road, but today it is more often used figuratively for the forgotten side behind a glamorous surface. You mostly see it in writing, news and storytelling.

examples.en: The neighborhood I moved to feels like a whole new world.

examples.ko: 처음 들어간 대형 서점은 책의 별천지였어요.
examples.en: The huge bookstore I entered for the first time was a wonderland of books.
For kids, an amusement park is a wonderland.

examples.ko: 도시를 떠나 시골로 오니 별천지에 온 기분이에요.
examples.en: Leaving the city for the countryside feels like arriving in another world.
When I opened the door, a whole new world spread out in front of me.

examples.ko: 겨울 산은 눈이 쌓여서 별천지로 변했어요.
examples.en: The winter mountain turned into a wonderland with snow piled up.

explain: 평소 보던 곳과 아주 다르고 신기하거나 좋은 곳을 말할 때 써요. 보통 '별천지 같다', '별천지로 변하다'처럼 감탄하는 말투로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The snow-covered mountain looked like another world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소와 아주 다른 곳을 보고 감탄할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to express amazement at a place very different from the usual.

phrases.example: 밤이 되자 거리가 불빛의 별천지로 변했어요.
phrases.en: At night the street turned into a wonderland of lights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곳이 전혀 다른 신기한 모습으로 바뀔 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a place changes into a completely different, wondrous scene.

phrases.example: 처음 외국에 가니 별세계에 온 것 같았어요.
phrases.en: Going abroad for the first time, I felt like I'd come to a different world.
phrases.nuance_ko: '별천지'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 분위기나 환경이 아주 다른 곳에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 별천지; used for a place with a very different atmosphere.

explain_en: It is used for a place very different from the usual that feels wondrous or nice. It often appears in phrases like '별천지 같다' or '별천지로 변하다', in an admiring tone.

examples.ko: 개울에 놓인 좁은 외나무다리를 조심조심 건넜어요.
examples.en: I carefully crossed the narrow log bridge over the stream.
There is a log bridge over a stream in the countryside.

examples.ko: 외나무다리에서는 두 사람이 비켜 가기 어려워요.
examples.en: On a log bridge, it's hard for two people to pass each other.

examples.ko: 외나무다리 위를 걸을 때는 균형이 중요해요.
examples.en: Balance is important when you walk on a log bridge.
It rained, so the log bridge was very slippery.
I took a photo of crossing the river on a log bridge.

explain: 나무 한 개로 만든 좁은 다리예요. 사람이 마주치면 피할 수 없다는 점 때문에 속담에 자주 나와요. 실제로 보기는 어려워서 말로 더 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: You avoided him so much, but you ended up meeting him anyway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피하고 싶은 사람을 결국 피할 수 없는 곳에서 만난다는 속담이에요. 실제 다리가 없어도 껄끄러운 사람과 마주쳤을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning you end up meeting someone you want to avoid in a place where you cannot escape. It is said even with no real bridge, when you run into someone awkward.
phrases.en_equiv: You can't avoid your enemy forever

explain_en: It is a narrow bridge made of a single log. Because two people meeting on it cannot avoid each other, it often appears in proverbs. You hear it in sayings more often than you see the real thing.

examples.ko: 집 한 채가 마을에서 외따로 서 있어요.
examples.en: A single house stands apart from the village.

examples.ko: 그 섬은 육지와 외따로 떨어져 있어요.
examples.en: That island lies far apart from the mainland.
The child sat off by himself and played alone.
It's a hut built in isolation, so there are no neighbors.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 마을 끝에 외따로 있어서 조용해요.
examples.en: Our house stands alone at the edge of the village, so it's quiet.

examples.ko: 그는 모임에서 외따로 떨어져 책만 읽었어요.
examples.en: He kept apart from the gathering and only read a book.

explain: 다른 것과 떨어져 혼자 있는 모습을 말하고, '외따로 서 있다', '외따로 떨어져 있다'처럼 자주 써요. 집이나 섬 같은 장소뿐 아니라 사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요. 비슷한 '외떨어지다'는 '외떨어진 곳'처럼 장소에 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 교실 구석에 외따로 앉아 있었어요.
phrases.en: The child was sitting apart in the corner of the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 다른 사람들과 떨어져 혼자 있는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a person who stays apart from others, alone.

phrases.en: Grandfather lives alone, away from others, in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마을에서 떨어진 곳에서 혼자 사는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes living alone, away from the village.

phrases.example: 의자 하나가 방 가운데 외따로 놓여 있어요.
phrases.en: A single chair is placed apart in the middle of the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 다른 것과 떨어져 혼자 놓인 모습에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for an object placed apart from others.

explain_en: It describes something standing apart and alone, often in '외따로 서 있다' or '외따로 떨어져 있다'. It works for places like houses and islands and also for people. The similar '외떨어지다' is mostly used for places, as in '외떨어진 곳'.

examples.en: In Byeoljubujeon, the turtle takes the rabbit to the Dragon Palace.
I read the story of the rabbit who went to the Dragon Palace.
They say the Dragon King lives in the undersea Dragon Palace.
In that cartoon, the Dragon Palace appears in a splendid way.
The children imagined the Dragon Palace and drew a picture.
I visited an aquarium as splendid as a Dragon Palace.

explain: 옛이야기 속 바닷속 세계라서 상상 속 장소로만 말해요. '수궁'이라고도 해요. 가게나 시설 이름에 쓰이기도 해요.

phrases.en: They say the Dragon King lives in the underwater palace.
phrases.nuance_ko: '용궁'과 같은 곳을 가리키는 다른 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another word for the same place as '용궁'.

phrases.en: I like the story of the rabbit going to the underwater palace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase that often appears in old tales.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the underwater palace

phrases.en: Grandmother told me a story about the underwater palace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기, 동화와 같이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with words like story or fairy tale.

explain_en: It is a world under the sea from old tales, so it is spoken of only as an imaginary place. It is also called '수궁'. It is sometimes used in the names of shops and facilities.

examples.en: Jeju Island was a fairly well-known place of exile in the old days.
We learned about places of exile in history class.

examples.ko: 유배지에서 쓴 편지가 박물관에 남아 있어요.
examples.en: A letter written in exile is kept in the museum.

examples.ko: 그분은 유배지에서도 책 쓰는 일을 멈추지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even in exile, he didn't stop writing books.

examples.ko: 유배지로 가는 길은 아주 멀고 힘들었대요.
examples.en: I heard the road to the place of exile was very long and hard.
Now that place of exile has become a tourist spot.

explain: 역사 수업이나 사극 이야기에서 주로 들어요. 사람을 보내는 일은 '유배'라고 해서 '유배를 가다', '유배를 보내다'처럼 말하고, 그 장소가 '유배지'예요.

phrases.en: The scholar was unjustly sent into exile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌을 받아 먼 곳으로 가는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person who is sent away as punishment.

phrases.example: 왕은 그 신하를 먼 섬으로 유배를 보냈어요.
phrases.en: The king sent that official into exile on a distant island.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌을 주는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the one who imposes the punishment.

phrases.en: That island was used as a place of exile for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소가 어떤 역할을 했는지 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain what role a place served.
phrases.en_equiv: to be used as a place of exile

explain_en: You mostly hear it in history class and in stories about the past. Sending someone away is called '유배', as in '유배를 가다' or '유배를 보내다', and the place itself is the '유배지'.

examples.en: The thief was hiding in a hideout in the mountains.
The police found the criminal's hideout.

examples.ko: 이 오래된 창고가 우리의 비밀 은신처였어요.
examples.en: This old warehouse was our secret hideout.

examples.ko: 고양이가 비 오는 날 은신처를 찾아 들어왔어요.
examples.en: A cat came in looking for a place to hide on a rainy day.

examples.ko: 은신처에서 나와 보니 날이 벌써 밝았어요.
examples.en: When I came out of my hiding place, it was already light.

examples.ko: 사람들은 폭풍을 피해 동굴을 은신처로 삼았어요.
examples.en: People used a cave as a shelter to escape the storm.

explain: 모습을 감추고 숨어 지내는 곳이라서 범인, 도망자, 동물 이야기에 많이 나와요. 아이들이 노는 '비밀 기지'처럼 가볍게 쓰기도 해요. '피난처'는 위험을 피해 가는 곳이고 '은신처'는 숨는 곳이에요.

phrases.example: 쫓기던 고양이가 차 밑에서 은신처를 찾았어요.
phrases.en: The chased cat found a hiding place under a car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨을 장소를 찾는다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, meaning to look for a place to hide.

phrases.en: The kids made a secret hideout on the back mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이들이 놀면서 가볍게 쓰기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Kids also use it lightly when playing.

phrases.en: The animals are looking for a place to hide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '은신처'보다 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say it than 은신처 in speech.

explain_en: It is a place where someone hides out, so it often appears in stories about criminals, fugitives and animals. It can also be used lightly for a kid's 'secret base'. '피난처' is a place you flee to for safety, while '은신처' is a place to hide.

t90.ax: The police found the criminal's hideout.
